chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Muʿammar al-Zayyāt, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him): A man comes to me and says, 'Lend me dinars so that I may buy oil with them and sell it to you.' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to borrow money to buy goods and sell them back to the lender?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by the reliable chain of Saffan and Isma'il ibn 'Ammar, illustrates the permissibility of a specific pre-agreed resale arrangement (often linked to *bay' al-'ina* or simple commodity financing) where one borrows gold to buy oil for resale to the lender. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares it 'no harm' (*la ba'sa*), affirming its validity in Shia jurisprudence as a legitimate commercial practice rather than a prohibited riba-based transaction, provided the terms are clear. This ruling is significant in distinguishing permissible trade from speculative uncertainty (*gharar*) in classical fiqh discussions.
